summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of chronic constipation, cerebrovascular accident with aphasia and quadriplegia, type 2 diabetes, and dysphagia was admitted after failing colonoscopy prep due to abdominal distension. Imaging showed marked colonic dilation without obstruction, free air, or ischemia. He remained asymptomatic with no pain, nausea, or vomiting. A colonoscopy was attempted but incomplete due to tortuous anatomy and poor prep. A virtual colonoscopy was performed, showing no obstructing mass. He was managed with bowel evacuation, continued PEG tube feeding, and medication adjustments, including temporary hold of anticoagulants. He was discharged to extended care with a stable condition, restart of warfarin and Plavix, bowel regimen including Miralax and Golytely, and follow-up on imaging results.
